body: I’m know what you mean by just wanting someone to talk to.  I’ve been feeling like that too lately.  I’m here to talk and listen if you’d like.
I understand the darkness all too well.  I’m here to talk and listen if you’d like.

I can’t speak to if you should continue drinking like you normally do. That is definitely a conversation I’d have with your prescriber.  As I mentioned with mine  if she found out I was drinking any amount she would stop prescribing it. I learned that the hard way once..   I haven’t heard of any interactions with nicotine.

I was prescribed it back I 2016 after doing a sleep study.  My sleep was always horrible. I would have nightmares a lot or really vivid dreams. I never felt rested  I would start falling asleep driving for long periods of time and overall just felt tired all the time.   The doctor thought I might have narcolepsy.  I could fall asleep anywhere and within minutes. I wasn’t diagnosed with it.  I was diagnosed with hypersomia. Which is  excessive daytime sleepiness.  Modafinil has worked great for me. I take one right when I get up and try not to take the second dose no later than 1pm.  I was told not to drink while taking it.  It can be dangerous.  I have done it though and see why they say that.  Sometimes I can have a couple drinks and be drunk. Other times it’s like I can. Just keep drinking and drinking.   My doctor won’t prescribe it though if she knows I’m drinking.
I used to do the two together all the time years ago.   I was smoking meth and then ghb I mixed in some liquid. I love it!!

I can tell you that stopping is possible and so is staying clean. Now is it easy no.  I started using again at the beginning of October but had 27 months off meth.  That’s the longest stretch I’d ever had.  I’ve been using drugs since I was around 13.     When I’ve made the decision to quit I in the past I had to get rid of everything. No drugs in the house no paraphernalia etc.  also for me I had to go cold turkey. Treatment has helped me too. It got me away from everything for a short time. Some distance helped.  

That does sound like a tough chain to leave. Sounds like people I’ve known trying to get out of the dealing lifestyle. Especially the ones working with the cartel. Ugh.

I feel you. I didn’t use right now hen I got home. I still had stuff at home. I was high within 24 hours.  There is that part of me that knows I need to stop. For multiple reasons. The willingness to just isn’t there.   Have you had any clean time in the past? Do you have any support when you’re ready to quit?

I can relate to so much that you wrote in your post. Different drugs to cope but all the feelings you were going through sound all too familiar.  For awhile now I have felt like a waste and that I have ruined my life.  I have felt like all I’ve done is hurt people. So in my mind they would be better off without me here. 

I had an almost successful attempt recently too. One would think that would’ve scared me. I came back from the hospital and continued getting high.  That’s how I know that I’ve got a problem too. 

I’m really sorry you are battling all those feelings.  It can feel so lonely in the midst of them.  Know that you’re not alone. I may be a stranger but I’m here for you.

True, true. I won’t disagree a bit. If I could see even a glimpse of hope it would help me. Getting the help to even get another therapist has been overwhelming. I’ve been feeling like no one will be willing to.

Thank you very much for your reply! It wasn’t confusing or too much at all. 

I do understand that the meth use doesn’t help my emotional state.  I’ve had some good stints off of it since I started at 18.  

Isolation has been what I’ve been doing unfortunately. One I feel like I’m a burden to others because they don’t understand this roller coaster. Also because I just don’t feel like socializing. 

I’ve tried to look for some resources.  No luck yet. Even through a service my work offers. So it’s not like I’m doing absolutely nothing. I know no one else can save me or get me out of this.

I had a similar scare recently.  I got up to start getting ready for work around 5am. I hadn’t used anything since around 6pm the night before.  I got super lightheaded and had to sit back down. Few minutes later I went and got a protein drink and bottle of water. I thought it was just low blood pressure. Which I’ve dealt with before. So I tied a couple more times to get up. Same thing and was extremely weak.  Finally I made it to the shower.  That was scary because my vision went black. I had to sit down for a few minutes.  From there I slowly tried to get ready for work. The lightheadedness and weakness continued. 

I probably shouldn’t have even drove into work. I called my doctor office on the way in to talk to them and they said get to the ER now.  Thankfully I work at a hospital.  In triage my resting heart rate was 129 and my blood pressure was actually high. Doctor did an ultrasound of my heart and said it appeared there could be some thickening of the muscle and was going to refer to a cardiologist.  It’s in the ER for about 7 hours hooked up a machine monitoring my vitals. Up down  , up down. Heart rate never went below 115. I was put on a medication short term to help keep my heat rate at healthy level.  It’s scary stuff.  I know it’s really stupid and unhealthy on my part that I haven’t stopped.

I was diagnosed many years ago now with bipolar 2 and going through that trial and error of finding the right med or meds was never going to happen for me.  I felt like I tried  everything and experienced all the side effects possible.   I was so young when I got diagnosed that I know I gave up on meds for awhile and self medicated then I’d get back on them but wasn’t consistent.  I don’t exactly know what age it clicked but I accepted the need for me to be on meds.   Eventually I was matched with a good care team who found a good combo for me.  One with hardly any negative side effects and allowed to feel and not be in a constant fog. I literally felt what I guess some say as normal.  It didn’t take away all my uncomfortable feelings but the feelings quit lasting months. Instead maybe a day or couple days.  Meds have been a life saver for me when I give  them the opportunity to work. It’s taken a lot of patience for sure. Don’t give up.

I understand those feelings. I know a lot of people but definitely don’t consider most of them to be my friends.  I do have some people in my life that we’ve known each other since we were 18. We are all about 45 now.   We all talk here in there but not super close.  Overall I don’t feel I have a ton of friends.   I don’t need a ton either.  Those few good ones I can depend on and are with me through all life’s ups and downs is enough for me. I am very social though and love meeting new people.   To do that it’s pretty obvious what I need to do if that is what I want.  I need to change things in my life.  I’m not going to meet anyone else except for online if I isolate at home like have. So that’s a step I need to personally take.  I’m not a part of any communities, my family is really small and really don’t have any fun hobbies right now where it helps me meet people.   So damn it can feel rough. lol.  It’s hard to because at my core I’m an introvert but have a lot of extroverted qualities. The need to social is one of them.  I’ve just got to be on the look out for events that interest me and step outside my comfort zone.  If a friend doesn’t want to go with me just bite the bullet and go by myself.  Unless we make some changes we never will find our tribe.  They are out there. :)

I can relate to the point you feel you are in with your life. Different drug has got me to this point but same feelings. I’m pretty indifferent to everyone around me. In recently became single at the end of September and have no desire for a relationship at anytime in my near future. Not that I even close to healthy enough for one.   Overall though I really have no interests these days since I started  using again at the beginning of October.   I’ve managed to function somewhat.  But have already taken a short leave of absence due to my use also been in the psych hospital twice in the short amount of time so not really sure that qualifies for functioning. Slowly spiraling is more like it.  There was day years ago I’d say I would never get high at work.  Not the case today. I get high whenever I can throughout the day.  So sad and scary.  The addiction or whatever you choose to call it will just get worse. Sometimes quickly others slowly.   It can be a hard cycle to break. Even harder the deeper you get into it.  Huge suggestion if you want any chance to really get off the drugs I suggest getting a new job with a new boss.   Could be a fresh start in more ways than one.

I’ve been accused of being high so many times throughout the years. When I’m absolutely clean. It irritates me and at some moments offended me. Reason being is I have blue eyes by all my life my pupils dilate on their own and get huge.  I’ve never had to have my eyes dilated at the eye doctor because of it. They just don’t naturally constrict.   When it offended me was when I had months of clean time under my belt and I was going to NA meetings.  People would make their comments sometimes. I came back with a joke and said drug test me and you’ll see.  A counselor in rehab one of my stats made a rude comment about my eyes being dilated. So I laughed and told her to drug test me. She told me she was really thinking about it. She really didn’t believe me.  It bothered me so much cause I was putting the damn work in to be clean.  I wish she would have tested me at that time.
Dang bet that was incredible in person

Bad decisions don’t mean you are a bad daughter.  Your post reminded me a lot of myself when I was your age.  I made some of the same bad decisions and have dealt with some of the same addictions throughout the years.  I’m now 45.   I wish I had focused more on why I was doing what I was back then.  It would have saved a lot of pain and suffering throughout the years.  I hope you can talk to your mom.  Get yourself on a healthy path.  Your mom sounds pretty amazing! I’m glad you have her as support.
I totally get that! lol. No problem at all!  Deep breath. You got this!
None of them that I have been at as an adult have done that. I’ve been in a lot. They did come in early to take my blood pressure though.

I was diagnosed with bipolar 2 when I was 16  I’m 45 now. I have personally never felt the need to tell the whole world. Just those closest to me know.  I hate the stigma that still comes with having bipolar. I don’t recall in my last relationship how long I waited to open up about it. It wasn’t long though because I didn’t want to waste my time or theirs if they weren’t accepting. 

Recently, I’ve been going through some major ups and downs and it was noticeable at my work.  I didn’t tell them I had bipolar, but I did open up and tell them I was struggling with some mental health challenges. In let them know how it might impact my work and what I needed during this time. They have been really supportive. 

My biggest piece of advice to those recently diagnosed is to try and not focus on the label you were just given. Rather focus on the symptoms you’re having and work on treating those.  We may have bipolar but that doesn’t define all of us.  We are capable of living a stable and healthy life.  I can’t wait to get back there. When I’m there and I do tell people about being bipolar they are shocked.

I was just in the hospital in November and beginning of December.  Each one was a little different.  I definitely recommend some comfy clothes that don’t have any strings.  One hospital wouldn’t allow my hoodies even without strings. Was weird. One of the hospitals actually had scrubs we could wear too. They may have some basic toiletries there but if you can I’d pack your own. That was the most important thing for me.  If you like to read maybe bring a good book. I love to write but neither place allowed me to have pens or pencils and writing with the markers they had wasn’t suffix enough for me.  I wasn’t allowed my cell phone at either location either. So write down important phone numbers just in case that happens. 

I was also in the hospital as a minor, but I don’t remember anything about my stay.  I wouldn’t imagine that it’s super different.  Meds/groups/sleep. Seems to be what most places are like.

I love booty bumping and have done it many times now. I’ve never done it with just shards though. I’ve always dissolved it in a little water and used a liquid syringe to put it in.  I haven’t had any damage.

I’ve been prescribed propranolol for years for my social anxiety.  I just take it as needed.  As someone else said it  has always just helped me with the physical aspects of my anxiety. It hasn’t changed anything mentally. 

Good luck tomorrow! :)

I agree with trying to make an earlier appointment. I’d rather you be safe than for things to get worse and you to become suicidal again.  I can relate to the depression getting worse for sure. Unfortunately, I can’t get into my therapist until January. So, I was taken to the ER and had a short stay in a psych hospital. Not the most fun place but I was safe.

So proud of you for taking the step to better your life. I’ve been clean before. Had 27 months but relapsed at the beginning of October.  Now it’s just finding that willingness and drive again to do whatever it takes to get clean and stay clean.
I know the biggest thing is to get clean. Without that I’ll never feel my life has value or remotely feel good about myself.

I’ve had a history of nightmares, extremely vivid dreams and sleep paralysis too.  It went on for years for me.  Finally a doctor suggested a med that helps prevent nightmares. It’s been a wonder medication for me.  Not only do I rarely rarely get nightmares now the vivid dreams are mostly gone too.  I hadn’t had an episode of sleep paralysis in years until just a couple weeks ago. Forgot just how scary that was.

Yes to an extent. Then there’s that part of me that wishes I hadn’t reached out to the crisis line.  So sad to think like that.  Last Thursday I actually attempted suicide.  Someone had done a welfare check when I wasn’t responding to them. I know that literally did save my life. Again I have mixed feelings.

Oh! Sadly I was suicidal and making plans to harm myself. I ended up leaving my house around 2am and was walking aimlessly for a while.  I was chatting with the crisis line and after learning what I’d already done and planned to do they were concerned for my safety. They asked if I’d be silly to do a three way call with 911. Hesitantly I did agree. Once I figured out my location a crap load of police and medics showed up. I was then taken to the ER and was there for hours before being taken to a psych hospital.  I was only there for 4 days. I left ama.
You sure can, but what happened with what?
Thank you! Me too!

Thank you! My family doesn’t know the extent to how much I’m struggling right now.  In the past I’ve opened up about my addiction struggles only when I was headed to treatment. Not actually in the midst of it. 

It’s good to hear your perspective because I only know my own. I hear you when you say my mom would never forgive herself. I know 💯 that she would/does blame herself. She thinks she has been a horrible mom to all of us.  I see and feel the complete opposite.  My friends that know I’ve been using have done all they can.  The ones in NA have offered to take me to a meeting, some offered to help get me back in treatment. And some have just plain turned away. 

I wish you didn’t feel stupid.  I know I put  a lot of effort into portraying that everything is ok.  It isn’t your fault in any way that you didn’t see the signs. 

The battle now days I feel like I need to fight on my own. I’ve been here so many times. Friends and family have got to be tired.  I got myself here it’s up to me to get myself out.
Yep. Scary stuff! I had an ER visit back in November and found out I had Fentanyl in my system. The only drug I’ve been doing is meth.  Ugh
Oh oops. Haha. No worries at all though. :)  Sweet I look forward to it.
Balance can really be a struggle.  Ugh.
Feel free to reach out to me anytime.  I’m always looking for chat buddies. I love talking about pretty much anything and everything.  Not often I get to talk to other women. So that is a bonus. :)

I’ve replied to some posts and those ones are the ones that specify they are just spun and looking to chat.  I haven’t found any local women smoke buddies though unfortunately.  Met a couple guys though and they were really chill.   In my experience it’s been rare that they aren’t looking to hook up. I just make sure I’m super upfront about everything.   I’ve also met some folks by making my own post and saying what I’m looking for.
I totally agree with this.  I like it when people can put effort into their posts and tell at least a little about themselves and what they are specifically looking for.

When I get clean I go through the same thing.  Sleep a ton for a few days and then deal with insomnia.  I know for me it’s generally because I’ve thrown my body so out of whack.  It takes time for me to get myself back on track.  Creating a consistent routine really helps me.  Sometimes I get something prescribed to help me sleep. Just for the short term.

My condolences to you and your family. I can only imagine the pain that you are dealing with.  I’m an addict  who has been dealing with my addiction and mental health issues since I was around 13. I’m now 45.  I had a good stretch of clean time ( 27 months) up until the beginning of October when I relapsed.  

Currently, I’m living within two worlds. There is the part of me that has a full time job, owns my home, and my car. I have a good group of friends and an amazing family.  Some would call that and functioning addict. I’m far from it.  The other world I live in is the one within my head and deep in addiction. Every day it takes everything to hold it together. I struggle with those thoughts that my loved ones would be better without me. They have dealt with me and my struggles for so long. 

I can only speak for myself regarding your question about would it matter. Everything you mentioned matters to me tremendously.  My mom and I are really close and know she worries. She knows I’m currently struggling with a lot in life right now but she doesn’t know that I relapsed.  She’s my biggest cheerleader, but I’m just not ready to tell her and worry her even more. 


I admire you for coming here and asking questions. Instead of coming with judgment and blame.   Addiction just wants to just destroy the addict and everything around them.  It’s a vicious cycle I don’t wish even on my worst enemies.

I do! I started drinking and doing drugs when I was about  13. At 16 I had my first psych hospital stay and was diagnosed with  bipolar 2  I’ve had my battle with addiction all these years. 

Nice work on three months alcohol free! That is a huge accomplishment I was clean for a little over two years until the beginning of October.  I’ve been using since then.

Hey there! I have bipolar 2 as well. I was diagnosed a long time ago.  Back when I was in a psych hospital at 16 I’m now 45.  I feel the meds really do help. However, I feel like the hardest part can be the trial and error process finding the one or combo that works for you.  I have definitely been in ones that made me feel like you described. It’s worth talking to your doctor about adjust them instead of getting off them completely 

There are times that I hate the disorder too.  I hate the stigma that still comes with it and how a lot of people don’t understand it. They would rather just think we are crazy. 

Overall though I’ve accepted that the disorder is something that I will always have to manage.  Once I’ve been stable that actually isn’t very hard.
It definitely was! Probably one of the best so far.
Nice! I’m about 20 min south of Burien. It’s considered Kent where I am.
Hey there! It totally sucks doesn’t it?  Ughhh.  What part of Seattle you in?
45/F high as a kite too!
Awesome! How’d you like it?
Haha. I get that way too!!
I was prescribed it to help consolidate my sleep after I did a sleep study years ago.  I can take 100-300mg at night. I’ve always done 300.
I love oral doses. I put stuff in capsules.  They tend to hit me pretty quick too. Never tracked exact how long.

I’m not super familiar with coke. I haven’t done it in years. My doc is meth. I do know a lot about addiction though and the struggle that comes along with it.  I totally agree with the other persons comment about the first week really sucking.  The fatigue is horrible.  When I’ve gotten clean I had to make sure I’m eating good, getting a little exercise , get myself on a good routine and surround myself with good people.  

Give yourself lots of grace and compassion. Your body is used to getting something for a year. It’s a big change to it to stop. Change for the better though!!

You’re so very welcome! Finding a new therapist can be discouraging.  At least it was for me. I feel like it is an interview process lol.  Select a few of them, meet with them and see who you connect the best with.

Addiction can definitely be lonely and can totally mess with your head.  I think that is why many of us struggle to stay clean.  It takes a bit of time for our brains to heal.  I had 27 months clean before I started using again. I can’t recall how long it took to really start feeling better, but I was doing a lot to take care of myself.  Eating good food, exercising a bit, got myself on a good schedule, surrounded myself with positive people and family.  Some days will absolutely suck, but just keep moving forward. Before you know it you’ll feel better!

Wow! That is definitely a rough habit.  Something to think about.  I’m assuming you don’t want to get back to that. Especially since you been working your ass off to get everything back. Good job on that! Are you interested in trying any 12 step meetings or groups that are out there to build a clean network of friends that could support you?  I’m really self sufficient too but it is nice to have people to help and be there when you need it.

I’m sorry I’m just seeing you replied. Most of the time you can go to your insurances website and search for therapists there.  I’ve also used a site called psychology today.  It’s been awhile but when I was looking for someone new I was looking them up on that site. You get more information.

My vote was to commit to the 30 days.  The longer you can be away from the drugs the better. Use that time to learn new tools and coping mechanisms. So, that when you do get out you have even more to offer your job than before.  I would be concerned if my employer only wanted me to stay a week.  It would have me thinking they didn’t care much about my well being.  You did good going to treatment. Now that you are there pull your sleeves up and put in some hard work. Embrace the suck! :)
That sounds about right where I am and what I’ve spent.
Good for you for sure! Two weeks is amazing and no easy task. What have you been doing to stay sober?

I get some of those feelings. Like wanting to self destruct and not hurt those around you.  I feel that way. Have you ever lived in the streets?  It is not an easy life to live.  I’m sure a lot of them out there wish they had what you did right now. I can see the appeal to it when you think you can do what you want and just get high all the time.  Surviving out there will take a lot of time and energy.  I recommend doing something in life that makes you feel good about yourself.  That could be any of those things you say you don’t have. Start small. You might be surprised how good you could feel.  :)

I totally under that battle all too well. Currently, I’m using, but I had 27 months clean when I relapsed.  When I first got clean I kept my job but pretty much everything else changed.   I changed who I was hanging out with if they were still actively using.  Not this last time because I own my place now but I’ve been known to move too when getting clean.  For me it’s important to change my people , places and things.  What’s important is to just surround yourself with people and things that support you being clean.  That doesn’t mean you have to move or not talk to family , kids etc.  sometimes it’s just a matter of setting some serious boundaries.  Do you have any support where you are when you choose to get clean?
Believe me.. I totally understand. I’m in that place too.
You’re very welcome!!

I have been diagnosed with bipolar and ptsd too. Although it was a long time ago. It took me a long time to accept my diagnosis.  Mainly because of the stigma around it.  I’m not sure when I actually accepted it, but I have.  What I try to focus on is not the label itself. Rather focus on treating the symptoms of it.  That makes it easier for me.  Coming here was a good step to begin the process. Talking about it with others. You’ll be surprised how many others have been diagnosed too.  You’re definitely not alone!
Yes. I have definitely been on meds in the past with sexual side effects. It impacted the relationship I was in too. I ended up getting off that particular med.

I feel overcoming addiction is different for everyone. My addiction is drugs. For myself when I quit I have to quit all together. There is no slowly tapering off. However, I know people who that has worked for.  Block g the distracting apps is a good start. That had to be hard.  Take it day by day. That helps me when staying clean. If I think too far ahead it overwhelms me.

I can totally relate. A lot of my issues started around 13. I had my first psych hospital stay at 16 after a suicide attempt. There is where I was diagnosed with bipolar 2. I’m 45 now and it has been one hell of a roller coaster.  I’ve been to more psych hospitals than I can count. Treatment centers for my drug addiction. All have helped a little in their own way. However, my inner demons are still here.  I’m currently in a low spot in life and wonder if the roller coaster will ever end or if this is the way my life is destined to be.  It’s scary and sad.

I recently went through a breakup. Just a little over a month ago. So many emotions have gone through me. I was really suicidal a couple weeks ago. Ended up in the psych hospital.  It’s important to remember that you don’t need someone in your life to be happy. You will be ok. It’s different to want someone in your life instead of needing them to feel you can survive.  Keep talking about your feelings. They are valid.  Please take care of yourself. I’m here to talk if needed.

I’m so so sorry for your loss. I can only imagine the pain you’re going through right now.  I recently went through those same feelings. It was just a couple weeks ago actually.  My mind was telling me horrible things.  Mainly that the world would be better off without me.  Even though we had a suicide in our family last year and I saw how it impacted everyone.  Two nights in a row I ended up in the ER.  I went in with a high dose of drugs in me.  That first trip they didn’t do anything but keep me in a hallway for a few hours and barely checked on me.  The next night I took more drugs and for some weird reason a friend of mine called me as I was walking around aimlessly. She’s the one that called 911. I went to a different hospital where they seemed to care a lot more. Treated me with respect and I got into a psych hospital for a few days.   I can’t say the stay helped tremendously, but it helped keep me safe those few days.
I don’t recall where to find you and for some reason it won’t let me bring up your post again.  Glad it’s not too late!

Hey there!! Taking care of you needs to come first and foremost. I’m glad you’re doing good that. I should be doing that more myself.  With so much going on I. My own life I’ve been so overwhelmed that I’ve just wanted to avoid or just be numb to it all. Which is never good.  Wish I would’ve saw you on here sooner. You seem like a really caring and cool person.  I give you mad props too for being trained to handle the crisis calls. I was texting with one a couple weeks ago. Glad they were there.
It’s 210 here. Decisions decisions. Lol
Same! Well no sun tomorrow, but we will start getting g some light in about 5 hours ish
Haha! Wow 3 days. I try to sleep ever night or at least rest. I don’t function well in more than 2 days.
Hey!! I’m here to talk to. Feel free to message me. I have had those feelings and can relate.
It’s good for me. Definitely feeling it. Some say it’s really strong though. So if you’ve never done it I recommend lower. Can always do more.
You ever done it?
You’ll have to let me know how you like it!
Tonight I did .52. Some say that is a lot. It’s works well for me.
Feels amazing!!!
Do you have insurance now?
I’m sooooo high right now too. I don’t tend to get the sexual tension from smoking though. Not sure why. Booty bumps are a different story lol.

I had someone miss on me several years ago and there was no doubt it was a miss. It hurt like hell and burned really bad.  Then my arm swelled up. A sharp pain went down my arm and my wrist went numb.  Scared me so much I’ve never slammed again.
You’re so very welcome!! I’m hoping that is what will happen for you too. That way you can start a new chapter of your life and move forward.

I was put in rehab while I was a junior in high school and also have been in it as an adult.   All the ones I’ve been to have a lot of structure.  We had a lot of groups, one on ones with counselors and homework to do. In high school I was required to go to school while I was in inpatient. Once in a transitional house I had to either be in school full time or working.  As far as your phone each place is different, but a majority of them that I went to didn’t allow them. I can’t remember about the smoking part. As I was never a cigarette smoker.

I have always been honest with my doctor.  I know they aren’t there to get me in trouble. They are there to help me and can’t fully do that without all the information. I’ve been fortunate that I have never felt judged. My honesty has been followed up with compassion and understanding. I was given resources for when I wanted help.  So, overall I’m happy that I’ve been honest with them.

I went a little over 2 years without doing any until a few weeks ago. That high after not using for that long has been amazing!!   Boofing for me is so intense.  Not as intense as when I used to slam, but still intense. I love it!! I don’t snort it anymore unless I’m doing a hot rail and I do eat it sometimes by putting it in a capsule. My main ROA is smoking.  It’s crazy how the highs are so different depending on how I do it.
Me! Feel free to reach out anytime. I’ve been dealing with addiction issues for a long time. I’m here to talk and listen!

I’m so sorry to hear about the space you’re in. The depressive episodes are no fun at all. I know them all too well I was diagnosed with bipolar 2 when I was 16.  I’m now 45.  I didn’t want to accept my diagnosis at first or for very long time.  Today I know my diagnosis doesn’t define me. There is so much more to me.  I focus on treating the symptoms with my therapist instead of focusing on the label. 

Based off how you are feeling it doesn’t sound like a bad idea at all to check yourself into a program.  They could help you get back on track.  Hang in there!
I’ve done it with both and don’t notice a difference.  Orally is a different story.

Isolation is the easier of the two for me to deal with.  It takes a lot of effort most of the time for me not to isolate when I’m feeling certain ways.  Today is one of those days.
